record.notes: Royal Assent received on 25 November 2024 (S.O. 2024, c. 24). Order in Council 361/2025 of 28 January 2025 named 29 January 2025 as the day Schedule 1, ss. 1-16, the Enhancing Digital Security and Trust Act, 2024, came into force; it also brought provisions of Schedule 2 (amendments to the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act) into force on 29 January and 1 July 2025. The AI duties in ss. 5 and 6 apply only to public sector entities and circumstances prescribed by regulation. As of the e-Laws currency date of 9 October 2026 the Act has no amendments, and the only regulations under it are O. Reg. 51/26 (cyber security) and O. Reg. 52/26 (digital technology affecting individuals under 18), in effect from 1 July 2026; no regulation yet prescribes entities or circumstances for the AI duties. Section 12 provides that the Act establishes no private law duty of care.

verification.note: The stored OLA bill page and Royal Assent PDF confirm the title, Royal Assent on 25 Nov 2024 as S.O. 2024, c. 24, the AI provisions in Schedule 1, ss. 5-8, and commencement by proclamation (s. 17). Three stored Government of Ontario pages (ontario.ca, 14 Oct 2026) settle the status. Order in Council 361/2025 names 29 Jan 2025 for Schedule 1, ss. 1-16. The e-Laws consolidation (browser-rendered copy and print PDF) shows the current version from 29 Jan 2025 to its currency date of 9 Oct 2026, 'No amendments', and O. Reg. 51/26 and 52/26 as the only regulations. The ontario.ca EDSTA page (updated 7 May 2026) says those regulations take effect on 1 Jul 2026. The plain http copy of e-Laws is an empty JavaScript shell. ontario.ca is not yet in CA-ON known_hosts, so the evidence script counts its quotes as secondary.

judgment.status_reasoning: Rule: Schedule 1, s. 17 says the Act set out in the Schedule 'comes into force on a day to be named by proclamation of the Lieutenant Governor'. Event: Order in Council 361/2025 (approved 28 Jan 2025) names 'January 29, 2025' as the day Schedule 1, ss. 1-16 come into force. The e-Laws consolidation confirms a current version running from 29 Jan 2025 to its currency date of 9 Oct 2026, with no amendments; ss. 17 and 18 (commencement, short title) are shown as omitted, as usual. Arithmetic: 29 Jan 2025 is before today (14 Oct 2026), so every substantive section of the Act (ss. 1-16) has been in force for over 20 months. Status 'In force', date_in_force 2025-01-29. Why not 'Partially in force': no section is still awaiting commencement. The AI duties in ss. 5-6 are in force as law but bind only entities that a regulation prescribes. e-Laws lists only O. Reg. 51/26 (cyber security) and O. Reg. 52/26 (under-18 digital information), so none are prescribed yet; the notes say so.
judgment.scope_reasoning: In scope without a scope note: the AI provisions in Schedule 1, ss. 5-8 are an AI-specific statutory framework for public-sector AI use.
